hints: Look closely at the two curves and ask which enzyme reaches its flat plateau first as glucose concentration increases.
Remember that an enzyme that works fast at very low substrate concentration and saturates early has a high affinity for its substrate.
walkthrough:
**Read what the graph is really showing**

Look at the x-axis (concentration of glucose) and y-axis (activity). Both curves rise then flatten when the enzyme is saturated. Notice hexokinase rises very steeply and flattens at a low glucose concentration, while glucokinase rises slowly and flattens much later.

**Link early saturation to affinity**

High affinity means the active site grabs and holds glucose easily, even when there is very little glucose around. So the enzyme quickly reaches half its maximum rate and saturates early. That is exactly what hexokinase does compared to glucokinase.

**Pick the statement that describes the difference**

Hexokinase has the higher plateau (higher maximum rate) and saturates first, so it has the greater affinity for glucose. This matches the brain needing a constant glucose supply even at low blood glucose.

options.A: This is probably true for both enzymes, but it describes a similarity, not the difference in activity shown by the two different curves.
options.B: This is the wrong way round. Hexokinase flattens at a lower glucose concentration, so hexokinase saturates first, not glucokinase.
options.C: The hexokinase plateau is higher on the activity axis, so hexokinase has the higher rate, not glucokinase.
options.D: Correct. Hexokinase works well at low glucose and saturates early, showing a greater affinity for glucose than glucokinase.
